notes: Extracted from the guide and docs/evidence/transactiondetails.md at e7ed622. The evidence was checked on 0.1.78-c8526ae (25 October); its dbe0e02 section (#396, published 28 October) replaces the older sections where they differ. The guide's Sources were checked on 28 October on the installed build: jfs-components 0.1.78, mirror v0.1.78-dbe0e02 (Biscuit's main at dbe0e02, 27 October). Its TransactionDetails.tsx matches that section (on the web a list named by accessibilityLabel, each item named “label: value”, label and value defaulting to Label and Value); read from source, not run. The older Contract and Web render lines saying accessibilityLabel is never applied were not used: #396 was verified on dbe0e02 and closed. The guide names no other component to use instead, so the one avoidWhen rule (items that act) has no useInstead. Biscuit's Storybook page, as the evidence quotes it, also rules out the tappable row and a plan comparison; the guide does not say so, so it is not recorded. Examples follow the building rules: no Color Mode (the guide sets Light on every list), and the receipt screen drops the guide's Slot gap L on its VStacks. Their copy is the guide's own (the UPI and bank transfer lists, and the receipt screen's Title and Share receipt), with “Payment details” from In context; the transfer list is named “Transfer details”, the name the evidence's check used. Not recorded as a gap, per the pack's rules: on native the list is not accessible, so iOS probably never says its name (not checked on a device). Not recorded either: #396's MDX tokens and Code Connect points, which the evidence neither marks fixed nor still open now that #396 is closed.

evidenceFacts.name: accessibilityLabel
evidenceFacts.description: On the web the list is a list (ul, role list) named by accessibilityLabel, with no name without it. On native the list is not accessible itself (accessible={false}), so iOS probably never says its name (not checked on a device).
evidenceFacts.quote: Web: the list is `ul role="list"` named by `accessibilityLabel` (no name without it)

evidenceFacts.name: TransactionDetails.Item
evidenceFacts.description: On the web each Item is a list item (li, role listitem) named “label: value” (its own accessibilityLabel wins), its text hidden so it is read once, and not a Tab stop. On native each Item is accessible with role text and the label “label: value”.
evidenceFacts.quote: each Item is `li role="listitem"` named “label: value” (its own accessibilityLabel wins), its text hidden so it is read once, and not a Tab stop.

evidenceFacts.name: modes
evidenceFacts.description: No mode changes the list or its items: their tokens are one-mode collections of literals. The list passes its modes to its items, and an item's own modes win.
evidenceFacts.quote: No mode changes the list or its items.

evidenceFacts.name: children
evidenceFacts.description: TransactionDetails.Item children. Nothing truncates: long text wraps.
evidenceFacts.quote: No variants, no states, no truncation: long text wraps.

gaps.text: On the web, a TransactionDetails.Item on its own, outside a TransactionDetails, renders a list item (li) with no list (#413, Component Fix, To do). The guide never shows a standalone Item.
gaps.quote: a TransactionDetails.Item on its own renders an `li` with no list

gaps.text: Figma draws each Detail Item at a fixed 315 px; the package sizes items to their text, and the list fills its column.
gaps.quote: Figma's items are a fixed 315; the package sizes them to their text.
